questions.question: From whom did Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai acquire his Torah?
options: Hillel the Elder and Shammai the Elder
Rabbi Akiva
Rabban Gamliel
Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi
questions.explanation: Ribaz studied under Hillel and Shammai, and among Hillel's eighty students he was called "the least of them all."

questions.question: True or false: Among Hillel's disciples, Ribaz was classed as "the least of them all."
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The epithet apparently points to his being the youngest or the last of the disciples, and yet it was said of him that he left unstudied no Scripture, Mishnah, halakhot or aggadot.

questions.question: What title did Hillel the Elder grant him?
options: Light of the Exile (Meor HaGolah)
Father of wisdom and father of the generations
The Great Eagle
The Rabban of Israel
questions.explanation: The title defines him as a head of the sages and a guide for the generations to come.

questions.question: True or false: Ribaz taught: "If you have learned much Torah, take credit for yourself."
options: True
False
questions.explanation: He said the opposite: "Do not take credit for yourself, for it was for this that you were created." Torah study is a basic duty, not an act of personal heroism.

questions.question: True or false: During the siege, the zealots burned Jerusalem's food stores.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: They wanted to force the inhabitants to fight out of despair. Ribaz saw people boiling straw out of deep hunger, and understood that the city would not stand.

questions.question: How did Ribaz leave besieged Jerusalem?
options: Through a secret tunnel beneath the wall
Disguised as a Roman soldier
In a coffin carried by his disciples
Through an open gate, with the consent of the zealots
questions.explanation: He pretended to be dead, and Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua carried him to the gate, because the zealots permitted the dead to be taken out for burial outside the walls.

questions.question: Who helped Ribaz escape from the city?
options: Rabbi Zadok
Rabban Gamliel
Vespasian
Abba Sikra, the head of the biryonim and his nephew
questions.explanation: At the gate the guards wanted to stab the coffin, and Abba Sikra prevented it: "They will say: They stabbed Rabban!"

questions.question: True or false: Ribaz answered Vespasian immediately regarding the parable of the honey barrel and the dragon.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Ribaz was silent. Later sages criticized him for not answering: "We take tongs and remove the snake, and leave the barrel."

questions.question: What was Ribaz's first request of Vespasian?
options: "Give me Yavneh and its sages"
"Give me Jerusalem and the Temple"
"Release all the captives"
"Leave the Land of Israel"
questions.explanation: Thus he sought to save the sages of the generation and to establish a Torah and legal center in place of Jerusalem.

questions.question: For whom did Ribaz request physicians?
options: Rabban Gamliel
Rabbi Zadok, who had fasted for forty years to prevent the destruction
Rabbi Eliezer ben Hyrcanus
Abba Sikra
questions.explanation: Rabbi Zadok was a symbol of the righteous man who had fasted forty consecutive years, and his body was in mortal danger.

questions.question: What did Ribaz answer Rabbi Yehoshua, who wept over the Temple that had been destroyed?
options: "The Temple will soon be rebuilt, do not weep"
"From now on atonement will come only through fasting"
"We have one atonement that is equal to it: acts of loving-kindness"
"We will study the laws of the sacrifices in their place"
questions.explanation: He brought proof from the verse "For I desire loving-kindness and not sacrifice," and from Daniel, who engaged in acts of loving-kindness in Babylonia, where sacrifices were not offered.

questions.question: Which "good path" did Ribaz prefer among his disciples' answers?
options: A good eye
A good friend
One who foresees the outcome
A good heart
questions.explanation: "I prefer the words of Elazar ben Arakh to your words, for your words are included in his words": all the other powers flow from the heart.

questions.question: What did Ribaz call Rabbi Yehoshua ben Hananiah, according to Avot de-Rabbi Natan?
options: A threefold cord that is not quickly broken
A plastered cistern that does not lose a drop
Sin-fearing
The pious one of the generation
questions.explanation: The epithet points to his resilience and his capacity for leadership, even in the face of emperors and the sages of the nations of the world.

questions.question: True or false: After Ribaz's death, Rabbi Elazar ben Arakh went with his colleagues to Yavneh.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: He went to Emmaus, the city of waters and baths, and remained there alone until he forgot his learning. His colleagues prayed for him and his Torah returned.

questions.question: What was Ribaz's final blessing to his disciples?
options: "May you merit to see the rebuilding of the Temple"
"May it be His will that the fear of Heaven be upon you as the fear of flesh and blood"
"May you study Torah all your days"
"May you never quarrel with one another"
questions.explanation: When they wondered, "Only that much?", he explained: a person who commits a transgression says, "May no one see me."

questions.question: True or false: At the hour of his death, Ribaz asked that a throne be prepared for Hezekiah, king of Judah.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: According to the research, the presence of Hezekiah, who saved Jerusalem by peaceful means, was a heavenly seal on Ribaz's path.

questions.question: Why did Ribaz ask for "hatzalah portah" (a small rescue) and not the rescue of all Jerusalem?
options: Because the sages of Yavneh demanded it of him
Because Vespasian had limited him in advance to small requests
Because he estimated that a large request would be rejected, and then everything would be lost
Because he thought that Jerusalem was no longer important
questions.explanation: This was political realism: the emperor wanted a crushing victory, and Ribaz preferred a small but certain rescue of the nation's future.

questions.question: What was the significance of the answer "For I desire loving-kindness and not sacrifice" for the life of the people?
options: The abolition of the commandments between man and God
The cessation of prayer until the Temple is rebuilt
The transfer of the sacrifices to the beit din at Yavneh
The focus of atonement moved from the altar to acts of loving-kindness, in every place
questions.explanation: This was a far-reaching reform: acts of loving-kindness became the "portable altar" of the people in all the places of its dispersion.

questions.question: Why did Ribaz ask to save "the dynasty (shushilta) of Rabban Gamliel"?
options: To preserve a recognized national leadership and prevent anarchy
Because Rabban Gamliel was his son
Because Rabban Gamliel commanded the army
So that Rabban Gamliel would replace him immediately
questions.explanation: The patriarchal family of the House of Hillel was the legitimate leadership, and preserving it enabled the people to continue without a political center.

questions.question: According to the research, why did Ribaz weep before his death?
options: Because he feared that the Romans would persecute his disciples
Because he did not know whether he had been right in his decisions, as he stood before the King of the kings of kings
Because his disciples had abandoned him
Because he had not finished writing his books
questions.explanation: The doubt whether he should have demanded the rescue of all Jerusalem troubled him until his final moments.
